title: Underdog's Woof is a 32 MB speech model that runs in the browser
friendlyTitle: Underdog's new speech model is 32 MB and runs in the browser
summary: TechCrunch reports that Underdog has put a new text-to-speech model, Woof, inside a browser game at underdog.ai/escape. The company says the model is 31.7 MB, with 31 million parameters, and that it runs on most devices without an internet connection. In the demo, typing on a typewriter speaks the text back, and a tuner generates music. TechCrunch says the model is open for download. Founder Sigil Wen told TechCrunch he wanted local models so notes stay on the device, rather than a cloud notetaker. This follows Bark, a 167 MB speech-to-text model from the same company. TechCrunch's own caveat is the right one: a model this small is unlikely to replace a large cloud voice model, and it may still be enough for a local assistant or a short spoken clip.

whyItMatters: The test is the browser tab, not the parameter count. Type a sentence you care about, including a phone number or a name, and listen. If it is good enough, the text never left the machine. If it is not, you still have the cloud model. Do not brief a client on a 32 MB voice until you have heard the sentence you would actually send.
